How Do You Convert an Image to SVG Online?

Converting an image to SVG online takes three steps: upload a PNG, JPG, or WebP file up to 10 MB, choose a layer mode, and download verified W3C SVG 1.1 paths.

Online image to svg conversion reconstructs PNG, JPG, and WebP files (up to 10 MB) into W3C SVG 1.1 cubic Bézier paths with 0.02 mm contour precision and zero embedded bitmaps.
Drop your raster file: Upload a PNG, JPG, or WebP up to 10 MB into the image to svg workspace.
Pick an output mode: Select Cutout Color, Stacked Color, or Monochrome Line Art for your artwork.
Inspect & export: Recolor palettes live, verify clean paths, and download .svg or copy straight to Figma.
VERIFIED VECTOR GUARANTEES
True geometric <path> curves—zero hidden Base64 raster wrappers inside your image to svg file.
1 credit per verified conversion (3 free sign-up credits), with automatic credit restoration on failed runs.
Normalized viewBox and minimal anchor nodes built for Illustrator, Figma, Cricut, and React.
OUTPUT SPECIFICATIONS
Which Image to SVG Mode Fits Your Workflow?

Cutout mode is the recommended image to SVG preset for non-overlapping vinyl and laser paths, Stacked mode suits layered print artwork, and Monochrome mode traces crisp line art.

Comparison of image to svg output modes, layer structures, and target design tools
IMAGE TO SVG MODE	BEST INPUT	PATH STRUCTURE	TARGET WORKFLOW
Color Cutout SVG	Logos, badges, stickers	Zero-overlap punch-out fills	Cricut, Silhouette, Laser
Stacked Color SVG	Illustrations, icons, art	Seam-free layered shapes	Figma, Illustrator, Print
Monochrome Line SVG	Sketches, stamps, ink	High-contrast crisp contours	CNC engraving, UI icons
Batch Image to SVG	Icon sets & asset packs	Parallel queue + 1-click ZIP	Design systems & Web apps
